sentences.text: Shri Arun Katare - learned counsel for the petitioner.
Shri Jitesh Sharma- learned Government Advocate for the
ORDER 1.

The petitioner has filed this writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India challenging order dated 29/08/2017 (Annexure-P/1) passed by the respondent no.4 whereby he was dismissed from service on account of registration of an FIR against him and one co-accused person.

The petitioner has also challenged order dated 28/10/2024, whereby his appeal against the aforesaid order of dismissal has been dismissed by respondent no.2.
2.
The facts necessary for decision of this case are that at the relevant time, the petitioner was working as Head Constable at Ashoknagar.

An FIR was lodged against the petitioner and one another on 26/08/2017 alleging commission of offence punishable under Section 376(2)(n), 323,
506 and 34 of IPC at Police Station- Kotwali, District- Ashoknagar.
It is alleged against the petitioner that he remained absent from duty on account of registration of aforesaid FIR against.
Because of the registration of offence, the respondent no.4 passed the impugned order dated 29/08/2017 (Annexure- P/2) thereby dismissing the petitioner from service.
3. The petitioner was tried for the aforesaid offences in the Court of learned First Additional Sessions Judge, Ashoknagar.

Vide judgment dated 24/06/2022 (Annexure- NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31758 2 WP-5775-2025 P/3) passed in S.T.
No.80/2019, the petitioner and another co-accused were acquitted in the criminal case.
The petitioner thereafter preferred an appeal before respondent no.2 and requested for his re-instatement in service on account of his acquittal in the criminal case.
When the appeal was not considered, he filed W.P. No.8555/2023.

This Court vide order dated 14/09/2024 (Annexure- P/5)
disposed off the writ petition directing the respondent no.2 to decide the pending appeal of the Krishnaveer Dhakad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4036831/
1 petitioner by passing a reasoned and speaking order.

sentences.text: In compliance with the Court order, the impugned order dated 28/05/2024 has been passed by respondent no.2 whereby appeal filed by the petitioner has been dismissed.
Challenging these two orders, the petitioner has filed the present writ petition.
4. The learned counsel for the petitioner argued that the impugned order has been passed without conducting any enquiry solely on the basis of registration of FIR against the petitioner.
It is his submission that respondent no.4 erred in invoking provisions of Article 311(2)(b) of Constitution of India without assigning any reason as to why the enquiry is not practically possible.
It is his submission that impugned order of dismissal is stigmatic and carries civil consequences and therefore, could not have been passed without conducting the departmental enquiry.
He further submitted that since the dismissal order was based upon the registration of FIR, the petitioner should have been re-instated in service after his acquittal.
However, respondent no.2 dismissed the petitioner's appeal observing that the offence alleged against the petitioner was a serious one.
The learned counsel submitted that the petitioner was a confirmed employee of the respondent department and, therefore, merely on the basis of registration of FIR, his services cannot be terminated.
He, thus, prayed for setting-aside of the impugned orders and re-instatement of the petitioner with consequential benefits.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents/State supported the impugned order and submitted that the petitioner was involved in the criminal case NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:31758 3 WP-5775-2025 concerning serious offence.
He was a member of disciplined force and on the face of act alleged against him, he was not supposed to continue in the Police force.

He also submitted that in view of the petitioner's involvement in the criminal case, the disciplinary authority i.e. respondent no.4 was of the opinion that no further enquiry is required and invoking Article 311(2) of the Constitution of India, the petitioner could be dismissed from service.
It is his submission that since the allegations levelled against the petitioner were serious in nature, the action of respondent no.4 in dismissing the petitioner is justified.
The learned counsel also justified the order passed by respondent no.2 on the ground that the petitioner is acquitted in the criminal case as the matter was compromised between the parties.
Since it was not a honorable acquittal, the petitioner is not entitled to be re-instated in service.
He, thus, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. Considered the arguments and perused the record.
7.
Undisputedly a criminal case was registered against the petitioner and based upon the serious nature of allegations made against him, he was dismissed from service.
Subsequently, the petitioner has been acquitted in the criminal case vide judgment dated 14/06/2022.
In other words, he has not been convicted in the criminal case.
It is also not in dispute that before passing the impugned order dated 29/08/2017, the departmental enquiry was not conducted.
8. In the impugned order dated 29/08/2017, the respondent no.4 has unilaterally recorded a finding that the petitioner is guilty of offence in relation to which the FIR is registered against him.
There is no material to support this finding inasmuch as at that point of time only an FIR was registered against the petitioner and no finding was recorded.

In the impugned order respondent no.4 has also Krishnaveer Dhakad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4036831/
2 observed that conducting the departmental enquiry is not practicably possible.

,        NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025

(Dismissal from Service)          -

9.
From the aforesaid narration of facts, it is evident that respondent no.4 has recorded a finding that the petitioner was guilty of offence in relation to which FIR was registered against him.
The respondent no.4 has referred to provisions of Article 311(2) of Constitution of India while holding that it is not possible to conduct the enquiry.
The provisions of Article 311 of Indian Constitution are therefore, required to be examined.
10. Before adverting to provisions of Article 311 of Constitution of India, it is profitable to refer to provisions of Rule 14 of M.P. Civil Services (Classification, Control & Appeal) Rules, 1966.

entities.text: M.P. Civil Services (Classification, Control & Appeal) Rules, 1966
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Rule 14 opens with the words "No order imposing any of the penalties specified in Clause (v) to (ix) of Rule 10 shall be made except after an enquiry held .......".
It is thus clear that no major penalty can be imposed on an employee without conducting an enquiry.
There are certain exceptions to this rule as provided under Rule 19 of CCA Rules.

Rule 19 of CCA Rules reads as under:
"19. Special procedure in certain cases - Notwithstanding anything contained in rule 14 to rule 18 :
(i) where any penalty is imposed on a Government servant on the ground of conduct which has led to his conviction on a criminal charge, or (ii) where the disciplinary authority is satisfied for reasons to be recorded by it in writing that it is not reasonably practicable to hold an inquiry in the manner provided in these rules, or (iii) where the President is satisfied that in the interest of the security of the State, it is not expedient to hold any inquiry in the manner provided in these rules, the disciplinary authority may consider the circumstances of the case and make such orders thereon as it deems fit:
Provided that the Commission shall be consulted where such NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31758 5 WP-5775-2025 consultation is necessary, before any Krishnaveer Dhakad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4036831/
3 orders are made in any case under this rule."
11.

sentences.text:
The provisions of Article 311(2) of the Constitution of India, since have been relied upon by respondent no.3 while passing the impugned order, are reproduced as under :
"Dismissal, removal or reduction in rank of persons employed in civil capacities under the Union or a State - (1) No person who is a member of a civil service of the Union or an all-India service or a civil service of a State or holds a civil post under the Union or a State shall be dismissed or removed by an authority subordinate to that by which he was appointed.
(2) No such person as aforesaid shall be dismissed or removed or reduced in rank except after an inquiry in which he has been informed of the charges against him and given a reasonable opportunity of being heard in respect of those charges;
Provided that where it is proposed after such inquiry, to impose upon him any such penalty, such penalty may be imposed on the basis of the evidence adduced during such inquiry and it shall not be necessary to give such person any opportunity of making representation on the penalty proposed:
Provided further that this clause shall not apply- (a) where a person is dismissed or removed or reduced in rank on the ground of conduct which has led to his conviction on a criminal charge; or (b) where the authority empowered to dismiss or remove a person or to reduce him in rank is satisfied that for some reason, to be recorded by that authority in writing, it is not reasonably practicable to hold such inquiry; or (c) where the President or the Governor, as the case may be, is satisfied that in the interest of the security of the State, it is not expedient to hold such inquiry."
12.
It is thus evident that the exceptions to impose major punishment without conducting enquiry are similar in Rule 19 of CCA Rules as also under Article 311 of Constitution of India.

It is evident that the procedure as laid down under Rule 14 to 18 of CCA Rules can be waived only in a case where a Government servant has been NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31758 6 WP-5775-2025 convicted in a criminal charge or where the disciplinary authority is satisfied that it is not reasonably practical to hold an enquiry.
Even though the respondent no.4 has observed in the impugned order that conducting enquiry is not reasonably practical, however, it is not clarified as to why conducting enquiry was not possible.
Infact, there was no impediment in conducting enquiry against the petitioner.
Thus, none of the aforesaid eventualities are available in the facts of the present case.
Neither the petitioner has been convicted in a criminal charge nor respondent no.4 has conducted an enquiry before inflicting punishment upon the petitioner.
The respondent no.4 bypassed the procedure solely because FIR is registered against the petitioner.

The appellate authority also failed to exercise its jurisdiction without realising that the petitioner has been Krishnaveer Dhakad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4036831/
4 acquitted in criminal case.

sentences.text: Since, the petitioner was dismissed from service only because of registration of FIR, upon his acquittal, he should have been reinstated in service.

13. In view of the discussion made above, in the considered opinion of this Court, the impugned order dated 28/10/2024 (Annexure-P/1) and 29/08/2017 (Annexure-P/2) could not have been passed by respondent no.2 & 4 without conducing an enquiry under Rule 14 of CCA Rules merely on the basis of registration of criminal case against the petitioner.

The similar view has been taken by this Court in the case of Ravi Sharma (deleted) Through LRs (I) Smt. Aarti Sharma and others Vs.
State of M.P. & others (W.P. No.8489/2023) and Shailendra Singh Gurjar Vs. State of M.P. & others (W.P. No.28167/2019) .

entities.text: Shailendra Singh Gurjar Vs. State of M.P. & others (W.P. No.28167/2019)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the impugned orders, dated 28/10/2024 (Annexure- P/1) &
29/08/2017 (Annexure-P/2), are unsustainable in law and are accordingly quashed.
The respondents are, however, at liberty to initiate action against the petitioner for conducting departmental enquiry as provided under the law.
14. The petitioner's counsel argued that the petitioner is also entitled to full back wages and continuity in service.
However, it is worth noting here that the order of dismissal was passed by respondent no.4 on 29/08/2017.

The petitioner accepted the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:31758 7 WP-5775-2025 same and did not challenge it immediately.
He ventilated his grievance only after his acquittal in criminal case.

Therefore, since the petitioner himself did not take steps for challenging the order, dated 29/08/2017, for long eight years, the public exchequer cannot be burdened with payment of back wages to the petitioner.
Therefore, the petitioner is held entitled to continuity in service but without back wages.
15. With the aforesaid, this writ petition is disposed off.

(ASHISH SHROTI) JUDGE rahul Krishnaveer Dhakad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4036831/
